solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Ranting crowd in turn succeeded breaking into club (7)

indicatorNotes.in turn: turned round, the word runs backwards
indicatorNotes.breaking into: S breaks into the club, landing inside it

blocks.note: a mob is a crowd; turned round it gives BOM
a bat is a club, as in cricket or baseball
s. = succeeded, the abbreviation in family trees

annotation.surface: An angry mob barges into a club, shouting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ranting' is read as a noun here: bombast is ranting, puffed-up talk.
annotation.definitionFit: Bombast is pompous, inflated talk, which is what ranting amounts to.

entries.clue: I throw up over match official, one Simon (7)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, 'up' sends the letters from bottom to top
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, one piece sits over (above) the next

blocks.note: VAR = video assistant referee in football

annotation.surface: A sick fan throws up over the referee at a football match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Throw up' pretends to mean vomit; split it, and I + LOB go up the grid. Simon Bolivar liberated much of South America.
annotation.definitionFit: Simon Bolivar is the famous Simon of that surname, so 'one Simon' points to him.

entries.clue: Wildly enthusiastic about new libertine one found in bed (8)

indicatorNotes.about: to be about something is to be around it, so MAD sits round N

blocks.note: mad about something = wildly keen on it
a rake is a dissolute man

annotation.surface: Someone is besotted with a new rake they found in their bed.
annotation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not a bedroom one: the mandrake is a plant.
annotation.definitionFit: The mandrake is a plant, so one might be found growing in a garden bed.

entries.clue: Time to eat a very succulent growth (5)

indicatorNotes.to eat: AGE eats A V, holding it inside

blocks.note: an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: It is time to tuck into something very juicy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Succulent' looks like praise for a meal; it is the botanical sense, a fleshy desert plant.
annotation.definitionFit: The agave is a spiky succulent plant, the source of tequila.

entries.clue: Put fine glue on my doodah (9)

indicatorNotes.on: each piece is put on the one before, building the word in order

blocks.note: a fine thread is a thin one

annotation.surface: An instruction to glue a thin layer onto some gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: Doodah and thingummy are both words for something whose name you have forgotten.
annotation.definitionFit: A doodah is a whatsit, a thingummy: a stand-in name for an unnamed object.

entries.clue: Spender rarely missed beer, half of each (5)

indicatorNotes.half of each: only half of each of the two words is kept

annotation.surface: A man who seldom bought a round rarely went without his beer.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: a miser is someone who spends only rarely.
annotation.definitionFit: A miser is a person who spends as little and as rarely as possible.

entries.clue: Lose track of road kill (6)

blocks.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI in crosswords

annotation.surface: Losing track of an animal hit by a car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Road kill' reads as one dead animal; split it into two words. The M1 is Britain's main motorway, so crosswords often clue MI as 'road'.
annotation.definitionFit: To mislay something is to put it down and lose track of where it is.

entries.clue: Aimless wandering, concerned with earthquake (7)

indicatorNotes.wandering: the letters wander out of order

annotation.surface: Someone drifting about in worry after a quake.
annotation.walkthrough: Seismal is a rarer form of seismic.
annotation.definitionFit: Seismal means relating to earthquakes, like seismic.

entries.clue: Pipe up, rebel? (5)

blocks.note: a vertical pipe carrying water or gas upward, named for the direction it runs
one who rises up in revolt

annotation.surface: Should a rebel speak out?
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pipe up' looks like the verb 'speak up'; it is a pipe that runs up.
annotation.definitionFit: A riser is an upward pipe, and one who rises against authority is a riser too.

entries.clue: Los Angeles Gazette finally covers bridge game (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: take the last letter of Gazette
indicatorNotes.covers: LA and E cover CROSS, holding it between them

blocks.note: to bridge a gap is to cross it

annotation.surface: A newspaper in Los Angeles runs a column on the card game bridge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bridge game' pretends to be the card game; bridge is the verb CROSS, and the definition is just 'game'.
annotation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team game played with netted sticks.

entries.clue: Edges away, keeling over exhausted (3,2)

indicatorNotes.Edges away: the outside letters of the word are removed

blocks.note: keeling over = FALLING, whose edges are F and G

annotation.surface: Someone collapses and sidles away.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Edges away' reads as moving off sideways; it is an instruction to strip the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British idiom: after a hard day you are all in, with nothing left to give.

entries.clue: Displaced area in girl’s haunches and in the waist (9)

indicatorNotes.Displaced: the A is moved to a new place in MAID'S

blocks.note: girl's = MAID'S; its A (area) is displaced to the front, making AMIDS

annotation.surface: Something about a girl's hips and waistline.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'waist' is a ship's: the middle section of the deck. Only the A moves; the rest of MAID'S stays put.
annotation.definitionFit: Amidships means in the middle of a ship, the part sailors call the waist.

entries.clue: First person to go in to admire brown study (7)

indicatorNotes.to go in: to go in is to enter, so I enters REVERE and ends up inside it

blocks.note: to revere is to admire deeply

annotation.surface: A visitor is first in line to admire a study in a stately home.
annotation.walkthrough: A brown study is a state of deep, absent-minded thought, not a room.
annotation.definitionFit: A reverie is a daydream, the same lost-in-thought state as a brown study.

entries.clue: School music award missing year, a choir’s last (7)

indicatorNotes.missing: the award is missing the year, so its Y is left out
indicatorNotes.last: take the last letter of choir

blocks.note: GRAMMY, the US music award, without Y (year)

annotation.surface: A school choir misses out on a music prize this year.
annotation.walkthrough: A grammar school is a selective secondary school in Britain, so 'School' alone can mean GRAMMAR.
annotation.definitionFit: Grammar is short for grammar school, a kind of British school.

entries.clue: Sitting astride modest conveyance hard, a few make strong impression (6,4)

indicatorNotes.Sitting astride: SOME straddles TRIKE and H, one leg each side

blocks.note: a trike is a humble three-wheeler

annotation.surface: A few people riding a humble vehicle hard make a big impact.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sitting astride' is read with its subject, 'a few', coming last in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: To strike home is to hit the mark, making a strong impression.

entries.clue: Nothing is gained by hanging about and sucking up (9)

indicatorNotes.is gained by: HOVERING gains O, taking it inside

blocks.note: to hover is to hang about

annotation.surface: A cynic says loitering and fawning get you nowhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sucking up' sounds like flattery; it is vacuum cleaning (Hoover is a vacuum brand).
annotation.definitionFit: Hoovering is vacuuming, which literally sucks up dirt.

entries.clue: No end of obstruction for co-operating parties (4)

blocks.note: an obstruction is a BLOCK, which loses its end letter K

annotation.surface: Endless blocking tactics in a coalition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'No end of' usually means 'a great deal of'; here it means lose the last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A bloc is a group of parties or nations acting together.

entries.clue: Dispatch salad plant, having wrapped it (8)

indicatorNotes.having wrapped: something wrapped is enclosed, so CELERY is folded round IT

annotation.surface: Send off the salad greens once they are wrapped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' looks like a verb, send; it is the noun meaning speed.
annotation.definitionFit: Celerity is swiftness, as is dispatch in 'acted with dispatch'.

entries.clue: With order of merit covering uniform, eat soup (8)

indicatorNotes.covering: OM is laid over U, covering it up in its place

blocks.note: OM = Order of Merit, a British honour
U is uniform in the NATO alphabet; OM takes its place

annotation.surface: A decorated officer in uniform eats soup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' is part of the instruction: take CONSUME and put OM where the U was.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: consommé is one particular soup, a clear meat broth.

entries.clue: English vineyard’s white, a bit off (4)

blocks.note: a cru is a vineyard, from French wine terms; 's = is, joining

annotation.surface: An English white wine that has gone slightly bad.
annotation.walkthrough: The wine talk hides a colour: 'a bit off' means off-white, not spoiled.
annotation.definitionFit: Ecru, the colour of unbleached linen, is a shade just short of true white, hence 'a bit off'.

entries.clue: Stream smooth computer image (7)

blocks.note: an icon is a small image on a screen

annotation.surface: Streaming a slick picture on a computer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stream' looks like a verb about video; it is the small river Caesar crossed.
annotation.definitionFit: The Rubicon is a stream in northern Italy, famous from Caesar's crossing.

entries.clue: Powerful expression being cut back, aim only for resolution (10)

indicatorNotes.for resolution: AIM ONLY is resolved into a new order

blocks.note: to lop is to cut; written back, POL

annotation.surface: A forceful speech is edited down to a single purpose.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Powerful' is mathematical: a polynomial is an expression built from powers of a variable.
annotation.definitionFit: A polynomial is an algebraic expression made of terms raised to powers.

entries.clue: In a perfect world, I mooch around rear of house (7)

indicatorNotes.around: mooching around something means circling it, so DALLY goes round E
indicatorNotes.rear of: take the last letter of house

blocks.note: to mooch is to dawdle, dally

annotation.surface: Someone's dream is to potter about the back of the house.
annotation.walkthrough: To mooch, in British English, is to wander about idly.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'ideally, we'd leave early' says what would happen if things went perfectly.

entries.clue: Little pet I don’t know catches a church mouse (6)

indicatorNotes.catches: PUP catches A, holding it inside

blocks.note: a pup is a young dog
er is the noise of hesitation

annotation.surface: A puppy, somehow, has caught a mouse in church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Poor as a church mouse' is the idiom, so a church mouse is someone penniless.
annotation.definitionFit: A pauper is a very poor person, as poor as a church mouse.

entries.clue: I’m thinking black fury brings offence (7)

blocks.note: um is the noise of someone thinking

annotation.surface: A dark temper, the speaker muses, causes offence.
annotation.walkthrough: To take umbrage is to take offence.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, mostly heard in the idiom 'take umbrage', meaning take offence.

entries.clue: Overturn cage in middle of studio (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the cage is placed in the middle letters, so PEN goes inside UD
indicatorNotes.middle of: take the middle letters of studio

annotation.surface: Someone knocks over a cage in a studio.
annotation.walkthrough: STUDIO has six letters, so its middle is the pair UD.
annotation.definitionFit: To upend is to turn upside down, overturn.

entries.clue: Regret rounding on crowd manipulator (7)

indicatorNotes.rounding: to round is to turn round, so RUE faces the other way

blocks.note: a mass of people is a crowd
to rue is to regret; turned round, EUR

annotation.surface: A demagogue who rabble-rouses comes to regret it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crowd manipulator' reads as a demagogue; the definition is 'manipulator' alone, one who manipulates muscles.
annotation.definitionFit: A masseur manipulates the body's muscles.

entries.clue: Crew, you shouldn’t have giant fish (5)

blocks.note: to man a ship is to crew it
ta is British slang for thanks, as said on receiving a gift

annotation.surface: A crew is presented with a huge fish as a present.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have!' is what you say on getting a gift: thanks, or TA in British English.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the manta ray, with a wingspan up to seven metres, is one of the biggest fish in the sea.

entries.clue: Anomaly of one working behind bar (9)

blocks.note: bar = except, as in 'all bar one'

annotation.surface: An odd sight: someone working behind a pub bar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub counter; it is the preposition meaning except.
annotation.definitionFit: An exception is an anomaly, something that doesn't fit the rule.

entries.clue: Cold temperature on Scottish island, mostly fine (5)

indicatorNotes.on: C T is placed on (after) the island
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, last letter dropped

blocks.note: MULL, an island of the Inner Hebrides, minus its last letter

annotation.surface: A weather report: cold on a Scottish island but mostly fine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is weather talk in the surface; the definition is the penalty, as a verb or noun.
annotation.definitionFit: To mulct is to fine someone, or extract money from them.

entries.clue: One giving name getting through entrance (5)

indicatorNotes.getting through: N gets through the door, ending up inside it

annotation.surface: A guest gives their name to get through the entrance.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a doorman checking a guest list.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: donors give money, blood or organs, so 'one giving' fits.

entries.clue: Seriously hoarse, missing a line (7)

indicatorNotes.missing: the hoarse word goes missing a line, so one L is left out

annotation.surface: Someone is badly hoarse and forgets a line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seriously hoarse' reads as one phrase; 'Seriously' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: grave means serious, so 'gravely ill' is seriously ill.
